download.title: Download LivePlay
download.subtitle: Free and open-source. Available for Windows, macOS, and Linux.

macGatekeeper.title: macOS: "LivePlay is damaged and can't be opened"?
macGatekeeper.intro: LivePlay is not yet signed with an Apple Developer certificate, so macOS quarantines it on download. The app is safe — this just means Apple hasn't been paid to notarize it. To open it, remove the quarantine flag once after installing to /Applications:
macGatekeeper.outro: Enter your password when prompted, then launch LivePlay normally. You only need to do this once per install.

winSmartScreen.title: Windows: "Windows protected your PC"?
winSmartScreen.intro: LivePlay isn't yet signed with a certificate Microsoft SmartScreen recognises, so Windows may show a blue "Windows protected your PC" warning when you run the installer. The app is safe — it simply hasn't built up download reputation yet (code signing is on the way).
winSmartScreen.step1: Click "More info" on the warning dialog.
winSmartScreen.step2: Click the "Run anyway" button that appears, then continue the installation normally.
winSmartScreen.outro: If your browser blocked the download instead, choose "Keep" to save the installer first.

contribute.title: Contribute
contribute.subtitle: LivePlay is free and open-source — and always will be.
contribute.freeText: LivePlay is completely free to download and use — no licence fees, no subscriptions, no paywalls. Every feature is available to everyone, with no premium tiers.
contribute.licenseText: LivePlay is released under the GNU AGPL-3.0 licence. In plain terms: you are free to use, study, share and modify it. If you share a modified version — or run it as a network service — you must make your source code available under the same licence, so the whole community keeps benefiting.
contribute.contributeText: Anyone can contribute. Report bugs, suggest features, improve translations or submit code — every contribution is welcome. Head to the GitHub repository to open an issue or a pull request.

interface.title: Your Show, Your Layout
interface.description: LivePlay puts your playlist, cart player and mixer side by side. The Playlist, Cart Player and Mixer buttons at the top of the window show or hide each pane, and any pane can expand to fill the screen, return to your previous layout, or close. In the desktop app, the cart player and the mixer can each open in a window of their own, perfect for a second screen. Organise cues into groups: a closed group still shows which cue is playing and how far through it is, and a cart slot can hold a single sound or a whole group. Each computer remembers its own layout, so everything is where you left it.

mixer.title: A Real Mixer for Your Show
mixer.description: Send cues to buses, such as Music, Effects, Announcements, a subwoofer or the foyer, and mix them on channel strips with faders, mute, pan and meters. Any bus can be your Master, which feeds the main speakers, or your Preview, which feeds your headphones. A bus can feed another bus, go straight to a hardware output, or be heard only through its aux sends, which can be taken before or after the fader. Press PFL on any bus to hear it in your headphones, even while it is muted, without changing what the audience hears. Cues follow the bus of their group, so a whole scene can be assigned at once.

eqDynamics.title: EQ and Dynamics on Every Bus
eqDynamics.description: Open any bus to shape its sound. The EQ is a graph you can drag, with up to 32 bands of bell, shelf, cut or notch filters, plus separate high-pass and low-pass filters. A live spectrum analyser draws the sound behind the curve, before and after the EQ. Alongside sit an expander/gate and a compressor/limiter, with a curve that shows the signal passing through and gain-reduction meters, while stereo buses add width and bass-mono controls. The same view lists every cue feeding the bus, with its sends beside them and a mini mixer underneath for moving between buses.

routing.title: Hardware Outputs That Travel With You
routing.description: Your show refers to outputs by name, such as Main Out, Preview Out, Foyer or Sub. Each LivePlay server links those names to real sound card channels in Settings under Hardware Outputs, and one show can play through several sound cards at once. Take the show to another venue and anything that computer does not have is listed as missing: drag one of its outputs onto the missing one, save, and the show is ready to play. Main Out uses the computer's default sound card until you choose another. The links belong to the server rather than the show file, so every show in the same room uses them.

previewLtc.title: Headphone Preview & LTC Timecode
previewLtc.description: Line up the next cue while the show rolls on. The headphone button on any cue plays it through the Preview bus, and PFL on a mixer strip does the same for a whole bus, without touching your main outputs. The Preview bus has its own fader for your headphone level and a Mono button to check how a mix sounds when summed to mono. A built-in SMPTE LTC timecode generator sends timecode to the output of your choice, keeping lighting desks, video playback and other equipment in sync with LivePlay.

audioEngine.title: Robust C++ Audio Engine
audioEngine.description: At the heart of LivePlay is a dedicated, high-performance audio engine written in C++ that talks directly to your sound hardware — WASAPI on Windows, Core Audio on macOS, and ALSA on Linux. Every cue runs as a fully independent playback instance with its own decoder and fade envelope, so playing the same file twice at different volumes always behaves exactly as expected. The engine runs as a standalone server process: it can live inside the desktop app, or run headless on a dedicated backstage machine wired to your audio interfaces.

limiter.title: Brick-Wall Limiter & Loudness Targets
limiter.description: A true brick-wall limiter sits on every output channel, keeping your levels consistent and protecting your hardware and audience from runaway peaks. Choose from built-in output targets that match professional loudness standards — EBU R128, streaming, radio, Netflix and live — and LivePlay applies the right ceiling, metering zones and waveform calibration automatically.

meters.title: Broadcast-Grade Metering
meters.description: Trust what you hear with real-time, broadcast-quality metering at every stage of the signal path — per-cue, per mixer channel, and on the master output. Colour-coded meter zones follow the loudness target you've selected, so you can see at a glance whether you're sitting comfortably within spec or pushing into the red.

fades.title: Fades, Loops and Timing
fades.description: Every cue has its own fade in, end fade and Stop button fade, and a fade can be as long as the sound itself. Looping cues can crossfade their end into their start, so ambiences and beds loop without a seam. A cue can wait a few seconds before the next one starts, crossfade into it, or start it at a marker. Groups show how long they run and, while they play, how much time is left.

waveform.title: Waveform Trimmer
waveform.description: Trim your audio with precision using the built-in waveform editor. Set in and out points, adjust volume, and configure fade times visually. You can also automatically trim based on silence, or automatically adjust the volume so that all audio levels are consistent.

properties.title: Easy to use Properties Panel
properties.description: Change the name, colour and playback settings of each cue in one place. Set cues to loop, adjust their volume, choose the bus they play through, set start and end behaviours and trim silence automatically. You are in control of your show's flow!

ducking.title: Automatic Ducking
ducking.description: Configure automatic ducking to lower the volume of background music when announcements or dialogue play. Perfect for smooth transitions in live productions.

showMode.title: Show Mode
showMode.description: Switch on Show Mode from the header for a simplified, touch-friendly view made for running the show. Buttons and text grow larger, and editing controls are hidden so nothing can be changed by accident. Tap a cart slot to play it and tap again to stop it. It works well on a touch screen beside the desk or on a tablet connected over the network.

youtube.title: YouTube Integration
youtube.description: Download audio directly from YouTube with our built-in downloader! Perfect for quickly adding music, sound effects, or backing tracks to your show (please make sure you have the rights to use the content or are using public domain content).

settingsPage.title: All Your Settings in One Place
settingsPage.description: Every setting is now on a single Settings page: appearance, playback, audio and metering, the mixer, hardware outputs, keyboard shortcuts, MIDI control surfaces, the project, the server and accounts. Your own preferences, such as language, a dark, light or automatic theme, accent colour and meter display, are not saved in the show, and when you sign in they follow you to any computer connected to the same server.

accounts.title: Accounts and Roles for Your Team
accounts.description: Add user accounts and everyone signs in before they can control the show. Operators run and edit the show; administrators also manage accounts, hardware outputs and the server. Each person can add a profile picture, and administrators can export every account to a file and import it on another LivePlay server. Login stays off until you create the first account, and can be turned off again without losing anyone. Administrators can also see every person and device connected at that moment.

discovery.title: Automatic Discovery & Rock-Solid Reliability
discovery.description: LivePlay servers announce themselves on your local network, so clients find them automatically — no IP addresses to type in. If the audio engine ever stops unexpectedly, it relaunches itself instantly and resumes playback right where it left off, so your show keeps running. And because the engine is a true server, multiple clients can connect to the same instance at once — ideal for a primary operator and a backup, or a stage manager monitoring playback alongside the sound op.

remoteOperation.title: Local or Remote Operation
remoteOperation.description: The LivePlay audio server launches automatically alongside the application, or can run on a dedicated backstage machine with your audio interfaces plugged in. Connect from any computer on the same network and take full control: transport, properties, the mixer and live metering all work remotely. Several people can work on the same show at once, and every screen shows the same selected cue and the same Up Next cue, while each person keeps their own language and layout.

firstLaunch.title: Quick Setup
firstLaunch.description: Get started in seconds with LivePlay's streamlined setup process. Select a folder, create a project and start importing files! All your media gets automatically collected into one place so you can move your project between computers with ease.

ports.title: Network Ports
ports.subtitle: If you're running the server and client on different machines, make sure these ports are open on your network and firewall.

control.title: Control Surface
control.description: REST API and WebSocket connection carrying transport commands, project data, routing and live meters between the client and server.

discovery.title: Automatic Discovery
discovery.description: Broadcast and multicast beacon (group 239.255.69.80) that lets clients find LivePlay servers on the local network automatically.

ports.note: A single-machine install needs no configuration — the client and server talk over 127.0.0.1 and the Windows installer adds the firewall rules for you. These ports only matter when separating the control position from the audio hardware across a LAN.

settings.title: Where settings live
settings.subtitle: LivePlay keeps configuration in four places. Which one a value lives in decides whether it travels with your show, follows the person, or stays on the machine.

server.name: Server
server.owns: How the engine runs and binds, the venue’s named outputs, and the accounts
server.travels: No — it belongs to the rack

user.name: User
user.owns: Language, theme, meter unit and transport keys
user.travels: No — it follows the person to any machine they sign in on

project.name: Project
project.owns: The show: cues, buses, routing, fades and everything the audience hears
project.travels: Yes — this is the show file

machine.name: Machine
machine.owns: Window and pane layout, Show Mode, and which server this install talks to
machine.travels: No — and nothing about the show may depend on it

settings.note: A value that changes what the audience hears is never stored outside the show file. That one rule is why a show sounds the same in another building.

api.title: API & Automation
api.subtitle: Connect LivePlay to your show-control tools.
api.description: Control playback, edit projects and routing, and monitor live state over HTTP and WebSocket. When login is on, give Companion, a show-control system or a script its own API token from Settings, under Accounts, instead of sharing someone's password. The developer reference covers authentication, every endpoint, commands, events and integration examples.
